newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse automatic pilot stuck in 'up' gear.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse automatic pilot stuck in 'up' gear.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading shares is set to continue its record run on Friday after better-than-expected U.S. data sparked another Dow rally and sent bonds into orbit, dealers said on Thursday.
"If you look at what bond markets are doing, this market too has plenty of potential," one dealer said. "Perhaps is even 2,800 points a possibility," he said.
The Bel-20 gained 28.53 points, or 1.21 percent, to 2,391.23 to register its fifth record close in a row, after earlier setting a new intraday high at 2,392.82.
Dealers said that despite the high levels, shares continued to be attractive because of a lack of alternatives.
"In bonds you get a return of five percent a year, in shares you get it in 24 hours, just look at Colruyt," one trader said. Retailer Colruyt jumped 8.2 percent to 16,250 francs.
Some dealers were hampered by vertigo in their outlook but then easily reassured by the blatant lack of sellers.

Some shares, like chemicals firm Solvay fell victim to profit-taking but their weakness was expected to be temporarily. Solvay, which was still at 21,300 francs on May 30, slipped 0.8 percent to 22,950.

Colruyt was the flavour of the day, soaring on the back of rumours it might sell its Dolmen Computer unit plus the fact it had been lagging the market in recent months and analysts' recommendations ahead of the publication of 1996/1997 full-year results on June 26.
"Colruyt (share price) has not done anything this year although it's the only one among the Belgian retailers which can still increase its Belgian market share," one trader said.
Colruyt chief executive officer Rene De Wit denied that Dolmen would be sold but told Reuters it would be effectively split into two separate units from July 1.
De Wit said the split into two entities would allow Colruyt to sell the "external" part of Dolmen if that was required to ensure its expansion, but there were no plans for now to do so.
The "internal" part was vital for Colruyt and would never be surrendered, he said.

Chemicals and pharmaceuticals firm UCB, the star of trade on Wednesday with a 10.9 percent jump, added another 6.6 percent to 119,300 francs on a company forecast for another strong rise in profit and on stock split expectations.
